brief: Weekly GS note leads with an AI capex thesis: capex stays exceptionally strong but its growth rate should slow, with hyperscaler spend of $800bn (2026), $1.2tn (2027) and $1.4tn (2028). The key question is whether AI revenue justifies that spend; hyperscalers need roughly $300bn of annual AI revenue to break even, and monetisation is accelerating, with 48% cloud revenue growth in Q2 2026 and $1.7tn of backlog across the three largest cloud providers. US earnings are elevated but the team expects deceleration rather than collapse: S&P 500 earnings grew 51% YoY in Q2 on AI investment, semiconductor margins and investment income, and GS forecasts 11% EPS growth in 2027 and 2028, preferring hyperscalers and semiconductors. Separately, the note reports last week's tape: global equities rose 0.9%, led by EM (+1.3%) as Europe was flat; Technology (+3.3%) and Communication Services (+1.6%) led sectors while Utilities fell 2.5%. GS's 12-month targets: S&P 500 8700, 10Y UST yield 4.5%, Gold $5140, Brent $78, EUR/USD 1.12.
